api: Notion API for workspace content; AI features are primarily in-product.
cons: Only as good as the documentation behind it
Inherits permissive sharing as a disclosure path
Depends on third-party models, so read the sub-processor list
name: Notion AI
pros: Answers from the organization's own documented knowledge
No context switch out of the working document
files: Workspace pages and databases, plus uploaded files and connected sources.
value: Writes, summarises, and answers questions against the organization's own Notion content, respecting existing page permissions. Most useful precisely where a company has already committed its documentation to Notion.
engine: Third-party frontier models operating over Notion workspace content.
latency: Fast for in-page work; retrieval across a large workspace is slower.
quality: Good at summarising and drafting from source pages. Answer quality is bounded by documentation quality, so a messy workspace produces confident answers from stale pages.
tagline: AI inside the workspace, answering from the company's own pages.
use_cases: Answering questions from internal documentation without hunting for the page
Drafting and summarising directly inside working documents
Turning meeting notes into structured, actionable records
integrations: Connectors to common storage and communication tools
governance_note: Two points. First, it inherits Notion page permissions, so it will answer from anything the asking user can already open, which turns permissive workspace sharing into an information-disclosure route. Second, answers are only as current as the pages behind them: a superseded policy page will be quoted back with full confidence. Documentation hygiene becomes a control, not just housekeeping.
training_optout: Notion states customer data is not used to train models. Because generation runs on third-party models, the sub-processor list is the thing to read, not just the headline commitment.
